_what_this_is: Documents the working recipe behind scripts/demo/record-demo.mjs, which regenerates docs/demo.gif. Run `npm run demo:record` (after `npm run build:prod`) to reshoot it.
hard_constraints: Never write to docs/index.html, docs/card.js (other than via `npm run build:prod`), or any src/ file. The recorder only navigates and clicks real buttons on its own standalone rig, scripts/demo/record-harness.html — it never touches the committed interactive demo page.
scripts/demo/record-harness.html is committed so the recipe is reproducible without reconstructing it from scratch.
the_landscape_aspect_trick: The card's natural rendered shape (with the gallery strip enabled) is close to square — the orbit view alone is roughly as tall as wide, plus a nav bar. Recording at width:1000px with `setConfig({ height: 560 })` caps #solar-view's max-height at 560 — the square view shrinks to fit that height, leaving open background on both sides at the 1000px width. The gallery strip is `position: overlay` (the default), which floats over the view instead of adding to the card's height, so the box stays landscape whether the strip is open or closed. Recorded clip: 1000x598 (ratio 1.67), scaled down to 640x382 in the final encode.

harness_config.note: setConfig is called before the card element is appended to the DOM (createElement, setConfig, then appendChild) — calling it after connecting risks default_zoom being ignored on first render.

recorder.capture_method: Real screenshots (page.screenshot with a fixed clip) sampled at fixed points in a click/sleep/hold loop — NOT a synthetic cursor, NOT locator.click() teleporting. Motion in the gif comes from the card's own CSS/JS transitions (zoom-animator, twilight sweep) being sampled continuously, the same way the original recipe worked.
recorder.clip: measured once from #wrap's bounding box after the rig reports window.__ready, then reused for every frame
recorder.encode: ffmpeg two-pass palette (palettegen max_colors=80, paletteuse dither=bayer) scaled to 640px wide. 48 (the original) visibly banded the Sun tile's bright gradient into two hard rings; 96 fixed that but only fit once the zoom beat was cut to a single brief pulse. Restoring zoom to twice each way (below) reintroduced enough frames that 96 landed at ~1.06MB, over budget — dropped to 72, which came in smaller AND under budget (973KB) than 64 did (998KB): palettegen's color count and paletteuse's bayer dither don't trade off monotonically, since fewer colors can mean more dither noise, which hurts the LZW compression that follows more than the smaller palette table helps. Settled on 80 (928KB) for real margin against frame-timing jitter between re-records, rather than riding the edge of whichever count measured smallest this one time.

scenario_beats: gallery.mode is 'off' so the strip starts closed; open it off-camera, wait for at least 2 thumbnails to finish loading (no 'loading…' frames in the gif), then close it again before recording starts
hold ~0.6s on camera with the strip closed
click the gallery button — the real, on-camera opening click
hold ~2.5s on camera with the strip open, all 4 tiles visible (mymoon/moon/earth/sun) — the opening beat
hour-forward x14 (2 frames dwell each) — the twilight cone sweeps through a full day
day-forward x12 (3 frames dwell each) — the Moon swings through its orbit, planets creep
zoom-out x2 (2 frames dwell each) — pulls back to the outer planets
zoom-in x2 (2 frames dwell each) — back to default
hold ~1s resting frame before the loop point — ends on the orbit view, no gallery
known_risk: mymoon is sky-relative (skyFrame) and renders a 'No Moon Sky' placeholder instead of a photo whenever the Moon is below Chicago's horizon at the recording instant. `npm run demo:record` with no `--at` uses the real live clock, so a re-shoot can silently land on a below-horizon moment and ship a demo gif where MY MOON's thumbnail is a placeholder card instead of the actual render — this happened once already (2026-08-25T20:00:00Z, altitude -37°). Always pass `--at` with a timestamp you've checked puts the Moon above Chicago's horizon (41.8781, -87.6298): call `getMoonSkyAngles(date, lat, lon).altitudeDeg` from src/astronomy/parallactic.ts for a few hours around the target date and pick one with clear positive margin, not just barely above 0. Current recording used 2026-08-25T02:00:00Z (altitude +21°).
